summary: The candidate correctly repairs the DeepSeek CPU/AMX-selected and Ernie4 router fixtures and enforces FP32 at the CPU biased TopK boundary, but it is only a partial fix: Dots3MoEGate still emits BF16 logits and is rejected by that new boundary.

tests.what_was_measured: DeepSeek AMX-selected fixture and Ernie4 both emitted BF16; base biased_grouped_topk_cpu accepted BF16 and dispatched the mocked native op.
DeepSeek and Ernie4 fixtures emitted FP32, and the DeepSeek fixture bypassed packed BF16-output linear.
Dots3MoEGate emitted BF16 [11.75, 11.75] instead of FP32 reference [11.780056953430176, 11.775662422180176], then biased_grouped_topk_cpu raised ValueError before native dispatch.

tests.command: GPU linear_bf16_fp32 numerical reference fixture on candidate ed2ca323422f819e95fc8be3f3494df036d12b09
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI350X, output dtype was FP32 and maximum absolute error versus CPU FP32 F.linear was 2.5033950805664062e-06.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X executed the existing GPU BF16 x FP32 router-linear reference path; this is not Intel AMX evidence.
remaining_counterexamples: python/sglang/srt/models/dots3_common/modeling.py Dots3MoEGate still uses BF16 tiny_gemm_bf16/F.linear outputs. In the independently tested non-tiny BF16 F.linear path, candidate biased_grouped_topk_cpu raises ValueError instead of receiving FP32 router logits.
The optional specialized BF16 activation x FP32 router-weight AMX kernel is not implemented; affected FP32-weight paths use semantically correct but unaccelerated FP32 F.linear fallbacks.
remaining_limitations: The AMD EPYC 9965 host has no Intel AMX, so actual AMX execution, ISA use, and performance are unverified.
No affected full-model weights were available; no full-model, serving-path, or distributed claim is made.
The installed sgl_kernel native egg was used only for import-path inspection; no native source changed in the candidate, so no rebuild was applicable.
